title: Blueprints, Auras, Margin Notes, Sound & Pop-Outs
description: SMIL choreography from a timing chart, blend-mode aura surfaces, CSS hand-drawn annotations, semantic UI sound, and Document PiP widgets.

drops.title: Timing Chart Choreography
drops.description: One schedule array generates both the SMIL attributes inside three SVG scenes and the Gantt chart underneath them.
drops.concept: Timing charts are how motion designers plan a sequence; here the chart is the source of truth. The same rows produce chained begin="draw.end" syntax, an animateMotion run along a shared path, and a d-attribute morph — then render as bars with a playhead. Speed, pause and restart all go through the SVG's own timeline (pauseAnimations, setCurrentTime), so no script drives a single frame.

interaction.mouse: Scrub the speed slider to rebuild every scene with rescaled durations
interaction.click: Pause or restart the whole SVG timeline from 0s
interaction.touch: Same controls; the three scenes stack vertically on phones

drops.title: Aura Fields
drops.description: Four blurred colour bodies per surface, composited with one mix-blend-mode and contained by isolation: isolate.
drops.concept: Ambient gradient backgrounds have replaced hero images this year, and the good ones are not images at all. Each surface stacks four blurred radial bodies, blends them in a single mode, contains the blend with isolation, and finishes with an feTurbulence grain on overlay. Palette, blend mode, blur, spread and drift are live, and the generated CSS is printed beneath the layout.

interaction.mouse: Pick a palette, blend mode, blur, spread and grain and watch four surfaces recompose
interaction.click: Toggle the drift animation on the colour bodies
interaction.touch: Panel moves inline under the layout on narrow screens

drops.title: Margin Notes
drops.description: Hand-drawn inline annotations with no SVG per note — two borders make the elbow, a conic wedge makes the arrowhead.
drops.concept: An annotation should attach to the exact words it belongs to. This one is a single span with a data-note attribute: the curve is border-left plus border-bottom with a rounded corner, the arrowhead is a conic-gradient wedge parked on the end corner, the handwriting is content: attr(), and a feDisplacementMap on the pseudo-elements removes the machine-straightness. Direction, colour, marker and reveal are all custom properties.

interaction.mouse: Switch the note direction and colour; toggle the highlighter and the roughness
interaction.click: Replay the draw-on reveal across every note at once
interaction.touch: Controls stack above the article on phones

drops.title: Semantic Sound Cues
drops.description: Ten cues named by meaning — select, confirm, error, purchase, processing — each a Web Audio recipe rendered on the spot.
drops.concept: Interface sound is having a moment again, and the trick is naming cues semantically rather than by waveform so a whole product can change personality by swapping packs. Every cue here is synthesised: oscillator pairs with exponential decay, pitch sweeps, and filtered noise transients, mixed through one master gain with a live scope. Three packs re-voice every control in the demo panel, and the AudioContext only exists after your first tap.

interaction.mouse: Fire any cue from the grid, or use the demo panel's tabs, switches, stepper and buttons
interaction.click: Swap sound pack, set volume, mute, or start the looping processing cue
interaction.touch: Tap anywhere to unlock audio; every control is touch-sized

drops.title: Pop-Out Widgets
drops.description: documentPictureInPicture.requestWindow() takes real DOM — a timer, a sparkline and a checklist walk out and keep running.
drops.concept: Document Picture-in-Picture opens a small always-on-top window that accepts live DOM instead of a video frame. Each widget here is moved rather than cloned, with the page's stylesheets copied into the new document, so timers keep ticking and checkbox state survives the trip; pagehide moves the node home. Where the API is missing the same widget pops into a draggable in-page window instead.

interaction.mouse: Pop any widget into its own OS window, or drag the fallback panel by its bar
interaction.click: Click the same button again to send the widget home; only one widget is out at a time
interaction.touch: Falls back to the in-page floating window where the API is unavailable
